Mortgage Default Prediction Model Documentation

PURPOSE:
Predict the probability of mortgage default for new loan applications to inform underwriting decisions.

METHODOLOGY:
Logistic regression model with 25 input variables including credit score, LTV ratio, DTI ratio, loan amount, employment history, and property type. Model uses maximum likelihood estimation to estimate coefficients.

TECHNICAL DETAILS:
- Inputs: 25 borrower and loan characteristics from credit bureau and application
- Processing: Logistic regression equation: P(Default) = 1 / (1 + e^-(β0 + β1X1 + ... + β25X25))
- Outputs: Default probability score 0-100%, risk grade (Low/Medium/High)

PARAMETER ESTIMATION:
Coefficients (β0-β25) estimated using maximum likelihood estimation on 5 years of historical loan performance data (2020-2024) with 100,000 observations. Model retrained annually.

ASSUMPTIONS:
- Historical default patterns will continue
- No perfect multicollinearity among variables
- Logit transformation correctly captures relationship

UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION:
- 95% confidence intervals for each coefficient
- Hosmer-Lemeshow test for calibration
- AUC-ROC = 0.82 on validation sample
- Prediction intervals provided for each score

VALIDATION:
- Out-of-time validation: 2024 data (20,000 loans)
- Back-testing quarterly against actual defaults
- Sensitivity analysis on key variables
- Benchmark against FICO scores
- Stress testing under adverse scenarios

BUSINESS USAGE:
- Loans with default probability <5%: Auto-approve
- 5-15% default probability: Underwriter review
- >15% default probability: Decline
- Used for all residential mortgages >$100,000

MODEL GOVERNANCE:
- Documented in Model Inventory
- Annual validation by independent team
- Monthly performance monitoring
- Version control maintained

This is a statistical model that uses logistic regression to predict future default events.
